summary: Hermann Güntert worked in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Rostock from around 1921 to 1926 and at Heidelberg University from around 1926 to 1945.

Hermann Hirt studied linguistics and Indology at the University of Freiburg and the University of Leipzig. He served as Privatdozent at Leipzig (1891–1912) and as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at the University of Giessen (1912–1936).

Hermann Hunger, active in history, archaeology, and linguistics, studied at the University of Vienna, Heidelberg University, and the University of Münster. He held posts at the University of Chicago, the German Archaeological Institute, and the University of Vienna (~1978–2007).

Hermann Hupfeld worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Marburg and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, later holding posts at Marburg (~1825–1843) and Halle-Wittenberg (~1843–1866).

Hermann Jacobi studied Indology, linguistics, and philosophy at Berlin under Albrecht Weber and at Bonn under Johann Gildemeister. He held posts at Bonn, Kiel University (1885), the University of Münster (1876–1885), and returned as professor to Bonn (1889–1922).

Hermann Kulke studied history, archaeology, and Indology at Madras, Freiburg under Hermann Goetz, and Heidelberg. He held posts at Heidelberg University (1967–1988) and served as Chair of Asian History at Kiel University (1988–2003).

Hermann Oldenberg, a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Göttingen and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held professorships at Berlin (1878), Kiel University (1889–1908), and Göttingen (1908).

Hermann Olshausen studied religious studies at Kiel University and the University of Berlin. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1817–1821), the University of Königsberg (1827–1834), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1834–1839).

Hermann Osthoff, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Bonn under Hermann Usener, and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He worked at the University of Leipzig (~1875–1877) and became an ordinarius at Heidelberg University in 1877.

Hermann Sauppe studied linguistics, history, and archaeology at the University of Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann. He held positions at the University of Zurich, Zentralbibliothek Zürich, University of Vienna, Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium Weimar, and as professor at Göttingen from 1855.

Hermann Usener worked in religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Munich, Göttingen, and Bonn, and later held posts at the University of Bern (~1861–1863), the University of Greifswald (~1863–1866), and the University of Bonn (~1866–1902).

Hermann Wilhelm Ebel studied linguistics and Indology at Halle under August Friedrich Pott and at Berlin under August Boeckh and Franz Bopp. He taught at Gymnasium Schneidemühl and held the comparative philology chair at Humboldt University of Berlin (1872).
Hermann von Schlagintweit worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Munich (~1844–1848) and held a teaching post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1851–1854).
Hermanus Johannes de Graaf worked in the field of history and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (~1919–1935) and under Poerbatjaraka between 1927 and 1930.

Heymann Steinthal studied linguistics and philosophy at Humboldt University of Berlin under August Boeckh (~1843–1847). He held long-term posts at Frederick William University Berlin (~1850–1899) and the Hochschule für die Wissenschaft des Judentums (~1872–1899).
Hideaki Kimura completed doctoral studies in Buddhist studies and Indology at Taisho University, where he was also attested as a researcher in 1995.

Hideaki Nakatani, working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and computational fields, studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao, under Yutaka Ochihara, and earned a PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He was attested as a professor at Kobe Gakuin University in 2003.
Hidehiko Kurita works in religious studies and Japanology. He completed a PhD at Tohoku University and is attested as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University in 2020.
Hideki Kiyoshima, a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Delhi and served as a lecturer at Kindai University around 1988.

Hideki Yukawa studied at Kyoto University and Osaka University. He subsequently held academic posts at Osaka University (~1932–1939), Kyoto University (~1939–1970), the University of Tokyo (~1939–1950), and Columbia University (~1949–1953).
